args.lesson: Worked: I used three Bing FETCHes (HTTP 200) and parsed result URLs by decoding the ck/a u= base64. Failed: all three queries returned results that had nothing to do with the query. The exact-hostname query gave hyperallergic.com, the IWMS query gave temple.edu, and the bid/no-bid query gave generic UK pages. A challenge string was also present. So these unauthenticated Bing pages are degraded, and not finding our page there is weak evidence, not proof that it is unindexed. Raw counts of our hostname in the HTML only reflect the query being echoed back. Next time: do not use unauthenticated Bing HTML to measure exposure. The only supported exposure action is one IndexNow notification, and only on the next approved deployment (hash-correction digest d211ba68...).
